How we run the app:

- We start it with `bin/serve` from the project root and these environment variables: `RAILS_ENV=production`, `PORT=3000`, `SECRET_KEY_BASE`, `QUIZZY_MODERATOR_USERNAME`, `QUIZZY_MODERATOR_PASSWORD`.
- `bin/serve` prepares everything the app needs (the database, assets, and so on) and runs the app in production mode in the foreground. It listens on all interfaces on `PORT`.
- The app is served over plain HTTP (no SSL, no HTTPS redirects) and accepts any host name.
- `GET /up` responds with `200` when the app is ready.
- The app keeps all its data under `storage/`. It must not call external services.

Our QA auto-tests drive the app in a browser and rely on the labels in quotes in each task. Keep them exactly as written, as visible text, a <label>, a placeholder, or an aria-label.

The QA auto-tests also expect:

- Each item of a list (a quiz, a question) sits in its own list item or table row, with its buttons and links inside it.
- Switches are checkboxes (a styled switch is fine if a real checkbox sits under it).
- Confirmations use the browser's native `confirm()` dialog.

Moderators started asking for this:

> As a moderator, I want to reuse my quiz at another conference, or share it with a colleague who runs Quizzy too.

The quiz page gets the "Export" link. It opens a page that shows the quiz as JSON inside a `<pre>` element (the only `<pre>` on the page), ready to copy.

`/moderate` gets the "Import quiz" button. It opens a page with a "Quiz JSON" text area and the "Import" button. Importing always creates a new quiz, even if a quiz with the same title exists, and opens its page.

The format:

```json
{
  "title": "Frontend Fest 2026",
  "questions": [
    {
      "text": "Which HTTP status code means \"Too Many Requests\"?",
      "active": true,
      "options": [
        {"text": "418", "correct": false},
        {"text": "429", "correct": true}
      ]
    }
  ]
}
```

- `questions` and `options` keep their order.
- On import, `active` is optional (`true` by default), and `correct` is optional (`false` by default).
- The export always writes both, and it writes exactly these keys: the quiz title and its questions, nothing else. The export is only for moving quiz contents.
- Imported questions follow the same rules as the question form.

When the JSON is invalid or breaks a rule, the page shows an error and nothing is imported: not the quiz, not a part of its questions.

## Stack & Serving
- Ruby 3.4.4, Rails 8.1.4.1, SQLite3 (all database files stored under `storage/`).
- Propshaft + Importmap + Hotwire (Turbo + Stimulus); no Node.js build step.
- `bin/serve` prepares the SQLite database (`db:prepare`), compiles assets (`assets:precompile`), and runs Puma in production mode on `0.0.0.0:$PORT` over plain HTTP (no SSL redirect, accepts all host names).

## Moderator Area (`/moderate`)
- Protected by HTTP Basic authentication in `Moderate::BaseController` using constant-time `ActiveSupport::SecurityUtils.secure_compare` against `QUIZZY_MODERATOR_USERNAME` and `QUIZZY_MODERATOR_PASSWORD`.
- Models:
  - `Quiz` (`title` required) has many `questions` ordered by `position, id`.
  - `Question` (`body` required, `position`, `active` default `true`) has many `options` ordered by `position, id`.
  - `Option` (`body` required, `correct` default `false`, `position`).
- Question option validation runs on submitted form rows (`Question#option_rows`) inside a transaction:
  - Blank option rows are skipped.
  - Requires at least 2 non-empty options (`"Add at least two options"`) and at least 1 correct option (`"Mark at least one option as correct"`).
  - On validation failure, no DB writes occur and all submitted rows (including blanks, newly added rows, and checkboxes) are preserved in the re-rendered form.
- Dynamic option rows are handled by `app/javascript/controllers/option_rows_controller.js`.
- Active toggle on the quiz page submits immediately via `this.form.requestSubmit()`.

- Plays active questions in order (`quiz.active_questions`).
- Preview state (`step`, `score`, `picked_id`, `finished`) is passed via a signed token (`Rails.application.message_verifier(:quizzy_preview)`) in query/form parameters so no preview answers are stored in the database or session.

class QuizImport
  attr_reader :quiz, :errors

  def initialize(json_string = "")
    @json_string = json_string.to_s
    @errors = []
    @quiz = nil
  end

  def save
    @errors = []
    @quiz = nil

    if @json_string.strip.empty?
      @errors << "Quiz JSON can't be blank"
      return false
    end

    data = JSON.parse(@json_string)
    unless data.is_a?(Hash)
      @errors << "Quiz JSON must be a JSON object"
      return false
    end

    validate_payload(data)
    return false if @errors.any?

    create_quiz!(data)
    true
  rescue JSON::ParserError => e
    @errors << "Invalid JSON: #{e.message}"
    false
  rescue ActiveRecord::RecordInvalid => e
    @quiz = nil
    @errors << e.message
    false
  end

  private

  def validate_payload(data)
    raw_title = data["title"]
    if !raw_title.is_a?(String) || raw_title.strip.empty?
      @errors << "Title can't be blank"
    end

    raw_questions = data["questions"]
    if !data.key?("questions") || !raw_questions.is_a?(Array)
      @errors << "Questions must be an array"
      return
    end

    raw_questions.each_with_index do |q_data, q_idx|
      validate_question(q_data, q_idx + 1)
    end
  end

  def validate_question(q_data, q_num)
    unless q_data.is_a?(Hash)
      @errors << "Question #{q_num} must be a JSON object"
      return
    end

    q_text = q_data["text"]
    if !q_text.is_a?(String) || q_text.strip.empty?
      @errors << "Question #{q_num}: text can't be blank"
    end

    if q_data.key?("active") && ![ true, false ].include?(q_data["active"])
      @errors << "Question #{q_num}: active must be true or false"
    end

    raw_options = q_data["options"]
    if !q_data.key?("options") || !raw_options.is_a?(Array)
      @errors << "Question #{q_num}: options must be an array"
      return
    end

    raw_options.each_with_index do |opt_data, opt_idx|
      validate_option(opt_data, q_num, opt_idx + 1)
    end

    if raw_options.size < 2
      @errors << "Question #{q_num}: Add at least two options"
    elsif raw_options.none? { |opt| opt.is_a?(Hash) && opt["correct"] == true }
      @errors << "Question #{q_num}: Mark at least one option as correct"
    end
  end

  def validate_option(opt_data, q_num, opt_num)
    unless opt_data.is_a?(Hash)
      @errors << "Question #{q_num}, option #{opt_num} must be a JSON object"
      return
    end

    opt_text = opt_data["text"]
    if !opt_text.is_a?(String) || opt_text.strip.empty?
      @errors << "Question #{q_num}, option #{opt_num}: text can't be blank"
    end

    if opt_data.key?("correct") && ![ true, false ].include?(opt_data["correct"])
      @errors << "Question #{q_num}, option #{opt_num}: correct must be true or false"
    end
  end

  def create_quiz!(data)
    ActiveRecord::Base.transaction do
      @quiz = Quiz.create!(title: data["title"].strip)

      data["questions"].each_with_index do |q_data, q_idx|
        active = q_data.key?("active") ? q_data["active"] : true
        question = @quiz.questions.create!(
          body: q_data["text"],
          active: active,
          position: q_idx + 1
        )

        q_data["options"].each_with_index do |opt_data, opt_idx|
          correct = opt_data.key?("correct") ? opt_data["correct"] : false
          question.options.create!(
            body: opt_data["text"].strip,
            correct: correct,
            position: opt_idx + 1
          )
        end
      end
    end
  end
end
